limits: description checks are regex heuristics, not semantic. A sentence is excused from the stale check if it contains a change marker (previously / no longer / instead of / replaced / renamed / ...), so an inaccurate sentence that also contains such a word slips through; unusual phrasings of 'never expire' or of a fixed path can be missed; 'mentions' only checks for LOGSLICE_CACHE_DIR and a TTL/expiry keyword, not that the described semantics (precedence, default 3600 s) are right. Use the LLM judge (rubric.md) for accuracy.

limits: tests_untouched compares the PR-branch test files by test-function name (a missing test counts as kept if an added test in the same file has the same normalised body or contains the old name), count of non-constant asserts / pytest.raises, and added skip/xfail markers; it cannot tell whether an assert was semantically weakened (e.g. == changed to in).
